claims.text: In `sources/0809.2981v2.tex` (revision `source-revision-9f2d90286b159738da58b0fe0bd47f85b5597dcdbd2b987cea65817b43536281`, SHA256 `9ddef409b3aa44eb1d31f101f3d22b364fdb5b52c404bc06529a2e3f6441bb02`), the quotient \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) has \(\mathbb Z\)-basis \(\{s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). Exact excerpt: “the \(\mathbb Z\)-submodule \(I_{r,n-r}\) spanned by all \(s_\lambda\) with \(\lambda\not\subseteq(n-r)^r\) forms an ideal” and “\(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\) has \(\mathbb Z\)-basis … \(=\{s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\).” [source-2@L1318-L1330|claim=formal-document]

groundings.excerpt:
1318: The $\ZZ$-basis for $\Lambda$ given by the Schur functions $s_\lambda$ 
1319: has the property that the $\ZZ$-submodule $I_{r,n-r}$ spanned by all $s_\lambda$
1320: with  $\lambda \not\subseteq (n-r)^r$ forms an ideal, and the
1321: map sending $s_\lambda$ to $s_\lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ induces an isomorphism
1322: $$
1323: \Lambda/I_{r,n-r} \quad \overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow} \quad \ZZ[\xx]^{W_J}/\ZZ[\xx]^W_+ \ZZ[\xx]^{W_J} 
1324:                      \quad \left( \cong H^\star(G/P_J,\ZZ) \right) 
1325: $$
1326: Thus $H^\star(G/P_J,\ZZ)$ has $\ZZ$-basis given by 
1327: $$
1328: \{ \sigma_w: w \in W^J \}
1329: %  =   \{ \schubp_w: w \in W \text{ is }r-\text{grassmannian} \}
1330:   = \{s_\lambda: \lambda \subseteq (n-r)^r \}.

claims.text: For the bigrassmannian corresponding to \(i^j\), the source states that \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is generated as an ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by the interval-indexed set \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). Exact excerpt: “\(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is generated as an ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by … \(=\{ s_{\mu}: i^j \subseteq \mu \subseteq (n-r)^r \}\).” [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]

The supplied formal-source excerpts do not state that the degree-\(d+k\) columns are the direct-sum interval component \(\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r,\ |\mu|=d+k}\mathbb Zs_\mu\), nor that the *complete* \(h_1\)-row set is exactly \(\{h_1s_\lambda\}\) for all interval-indexed degree-\(d+k-1\) \(\lambda\). They also contain no bounded explicit Pieri-rule excerpt identifying those products as the requested rows.
